title: Time-Life Beiderbecke project and the lack of payment
summary: Sudhalter, working for Time-Life, asked for information without pay, which irked him.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Now, recently Time-Life has -- they're going to do a Beiderbecke thing and they hired Sudhalter (Phonetic) and they hired some other guy from the United Nations and he came up here. Then they got a lot of material -- the last time Sudhalter called up and he wanted to know about Bud Livingston. I said well, look, I gave him all the information I had, and I said, 'Hey, you're working for a big outfit -- at that time I would have loved to have something like that -- I said, 'Don't they pay anything for some of this information?' He said, 'No, that's the way they are.' I'll bet he's getting paid.
The guy who was out here, he sent my sister a

beautiful thing there. One of those books.
Let's see how. I had my interest in something --
Well, it must have been something but there were few and far
between, I'll tell you that. And nothing that meant anything.
Uninteresting stuff.
